name: run_gpnstar_vep
description: Score single-nucleotide variants with GPN-Star, a language model over a multiple-species alignment (human hg38, 100 vertebrates for the primary model). Each variant gets a log-likelihood ratio logit(alt) - logit(ref) at its position, averaged over the forward and reverse-complement windows: negative means the alternate base is less likely than the reference given the alignment, i.e. more likely to be deleterious. Coordinates are 1-based; chromosome names follow the alignment store (1..22, X, Y; a chr prefix is accepted); the reference base must match the alignment's human base, and a mismatch is refused rather than scored. Returns one score per variant in input order. The alignment store is held by the server operator: unless a full hg38 store has been configured, only the windows of the kit's eight example variants (chromosomes 1, 2, 3 and 5) can be scored, and any other position is refused with 'the alignment holds no data'. SNVs only: no indels.

variants.description: The variants to score, in the order the scores come back. At most 2048 per call.

chrom.description: Chromosome as the alignment store names it, e.g. "1" or "X" ("chr1" is accepted).

ref.description: Reference base, which must equal the alignment's human base at this position.

window_size.description: Alignment columns read around each variant (even). The primary model's native window is 128. Peak GPU memory follows batch_size x window_size, which may not exceed 8192; variants x window_size may not exceed 524288.

batch_size.description: Variants per forward pass. Does not change the scores' meaning; it trades memory for speed. batch_size x window_size may not exceed 8192.

ids.description: chrom:pos:ref>alt for each variant, in input order.

scores.description: logit(alt) - logit(ref), mean of both strands.

single_variant_sent_twice.description: True when the call held one variant: upstream's own command fails on a one-row table, so the variant was scored in a batch of two copies and the first score kept.
